upload_summary.note: the push reported 'Uploading LFS objects: 100% (1872/1872), 4.9 GB'. The count is below 1,900 because identical objects are stored once: the 1,899 captures plus the corrected book object are 1,900 logical files, and 1,872 distinct objects were transferred.

excluded.reason: captures of a different book; not part of the Book 2 reconstruction

sample_pull.method: CORRECTED: this entry originally described `git lfs fetch --include oid=...`, which is not a valid selector (--include takes paths, not object ids). That call was a no-op and the 12 hashes were read from the local LFS cache, not from the server. The genuine remote pull is recorded in reports/printed_contents_qa.json and contents_wave/remote_verification.json: a fresh clone with a sparse checkout of 12 real capture paths (spread across every batch) plus the book itself, so git-lfs downloaded the objects from the GitHub endpoint; all 12 hashed to their manifest SHA-256 and the book hashed to the local final.

clean_clone_check.method: fresh git clone of https://github.com/mhyahya854/AP, sparse checkout of two captures and the book, then SHA-256

not_verified: GitHub does not expose the account's current LFS storage and bandwidth totals through git; the storage figures above are computed from the uploaded object sizes, not read back from the account.
GitHub's web viewer will not render the 1.13 GB book or the full-resolution captures in the browser; both must be fetched with git lfs as documented in README.md.
